Opinion: ‘Dragon Ball Super’s’ new look is refreshing

“Dragon Ball Super: Beerus” trailer gives fans a continuation of the beloved series
Leandro Cervantes, Staff Reporter • Sep 22, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:46
Instaread
(Lucas Ramos / Golden Gate Xpress)
An illustration depicting a poorly drawn Goku losing a battle against a properly drawn Goku with red hair.

After an eight year absence, “Dragon Ball Super” is back with a renovated animation style. Toei Animation released a trailer on Sept. 2, teasing the release of “Dragon Ball Super: Beerus”.

Since its release, the trailer has gained millions of views and introduced fans to enhanced visuals and theme songs by MEGATERA･ZERO.

In “Dragon Ball Super: Beerus”, Toei prioritized showcasing new footage, clearer dialogue and enhanced visuals in an effort to honor the original series. 

The story picks up several years after Goku defeats Majin Buu and looks to face Beerus, the god of destruction.

While returning to the series after nearly a decade could easily have fans reeling for context, Toei Animation masterfully revamps the original in “Dragon Ball Super: Beerus”. Toei is no stranger to stunning animation, producing iconic anime series One Piece, Sailor Moon, Castle in the Sky and countless others.

Following the death of Akira Toriyama, creator of “Dragon Ball”, Tadayoshi Yamamuro takes the reins as animation character designer and general animation director, with Matsuto Seya as the head of series composition and direction arrangement. Yamamuro and Seya both have skin in the game with the series, with Yamamuro working closely with Toriyama on “Dragon Ball Super’s” original 2015 release and Seya continuing his storied career with Toei. “Dragon Ball Super: Beerus” will revisit where the 2015 series left off, starting with the god of destruction, Beerus. 

The question on many fans’ minds is why are they getting a re-release of an anime they’ve already seen?

The simple answer is they’re not. During the anime’s initial release in October 2015, many fans noticed the visuals had quality issues. Compared to “Dragon Ball Super’s” predecessor, “Dragon Ball Z”, the animation was noticeably weaker. For many fans, this realization came as the show introduced Goku and his friends after defeating Majin Buu in season two episode 66. 

However, the re-animation of the beloved series is a chance for Toei Animation to refine the artwork. In the last iteration of “Dragon Ball Super”, the animation’s inconsistency was one of the major criticisms the series faced due to sloppy details, lopsided characters and overly stiff movement. These details were noticeable as distinct characters were animated inconsistently. Across the board, fans pointed to the animation style as an issue. 

Lavell Nero is one of many fans who took issue with the series’ early animation. Nero found his expectations shattered following its initial release.

“It also gave fans a constant string of heartbreaks when the animation failed to live up to expectation,” Nero writes. “Despite the fact that the series was now being produced in a climate that pressured animators more than ever to meet unrealistic deadlines, fans complained about the use of reused frames and off-kilter character models.” 

When comparing teasers of “Dragon Ball Super: Beerus”  to the 2015 release, the visuals are night and day. The features have altered details that are more distinct, the frames are clearer in the action scenes, and the colors are punchier. A mere eight years in the future, the two anime could not be more different. 

According to an interview with Anime News Network, Yamamuro talks about “Dragon Ball Z Kai”, a project he worked on to reanimate the anime to a more modern look. 

“Kai was incredibly positive for the franchise, because it gave us a great starting point for every new ‘Dragon Ball’ production going forward,” Yamamuro said.

Growing up watching “Dragon Ball”, this re-release makes me nostalgic for the experiences I had watching the original series. As a long time “Dragon Ball” fan, the stories were always compelling, but the plot holes and inconsistent animation often made the series overly confusing. 

When the original “Dragon Ball Super” came out in late 2015, the production teams at Toei were simultaneously occupied with large-scale projects like One Piece. Many speculate that animators were on tight deadlines and overworked

During this time, the studio was rushed to respond to the box office success of Dragon Ball Z: Resurrection of F, making over $61,768,190 worldwide on its original release.

The studio’s failure to juggle animators between projects led to the production of “Dragon Ball Super” being rushed. While “Dragon Ball Super” visuals were bad, there were improvements towards the end, but they were often minor.

In October, fans will be able to relive the glory of the original series and see long-awaited scenes animated. Given “Dragon Ball’s” decades-long popularity and the delay of the revamp, the storytelling potential is far from over.

“Dragon Ball Super: Beerus” will have its exclusive world premiere at New York Comic Con on Oct. 8, 2026. For viewers unable to attend the premiere, the series will be available to stream from home on Crunchyroll beginning Oct. 11, 2026.

Leandro Cervantes, Staff Reporter
Leandro Cervantes (He/Him) is a reporter for The Golden Gate Express. He is majoring in Journalism and minoring in Latin Studies. He was born in Walnut Creek but grew up in San Pablo, where he currently lives. He previously worked for The Advocate, the student newspaper of Contra Costa College.
